channel.title: Trend Reader
channel.description: The AI vocabulary, mapped: a weekly brief on the terms and themes to know, and every new term as it is defined.

item.title: Weekly brief, week W39: Price of the frontier resets, but the bill is set by effort and cache
item.description: This week's terms: Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Luna. Themes: Price of the frontier resets, but the bill is set by effort and cache; The harness is now measured, priced and trained; The score belongs partly to the scaffolding; Self-improvement claims moved from the model to its inputs; Agent load rotates the scarce input and pushes containment into the platform.

item.title: Weekly brief, week W39: The unit of competition is the system around the model
item.description: This week's terms: none new. Themes: The unit of competition is the system around the model; Two markets, tokens and revenue; Output per scarce input is the unit; The safety story matured to a governance floor; Benchmarks: measurement quality, not direction.

item.title: New term: Antitrust exemption
item.description: An antitrust exemption is a carve-out from competition law that would let rival AI labs coordinate on safety, such as cross-testing each other's models, agreeing release timing or a coordinated slowdown, without exposure to liability for restraint of trade. It matters because its absence is now a documented obstacle to safety cooperation that both labs and regulators have run into.

item.title: New term: Capability overhang
item.description: A capability overhang is the gap between what already-deployed AI models can do and what their users and buyers actually get out of them. It matters because the value locked in existing models would take years to absorb even if progress stopped, and because it lowers the premium anyone can charge for holding the frontier.

item.title: New term: Claude Opus 5.5
item.description: Claude Opus 5.5 is Anthropic's first Claude 5.5 model, released on 22 September 2026 at $4 and $20 per million tokens with cache reads cut 60 percent, the first price cut in the Opus line's history. It matters because Anthropic claims Fable 5.1-level quality at 40 percent lower cost, which reset the price of frontier-grade capability in the same week as OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol and Luna.

item.title: New term: Embedded evaluators
item.description: Embedded evaluators are independent third-party staff placed inside a frontier lab with employee-like access to models, training runs and incidents, and the right to publish what they find. They matter because they are the concrete oversight mechanism labs have committed to in place of external regulation, and their supply, independence and political acceptability are all in question.

item.title: New term: GPT-6 Luna
item.description: GPT-6 Luna is the cheapest tier of OpenAI's GPT-6 family, released on 22 September 2026 at $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens, a price OpenAI states is permanent. It matters because it puts near-frontier coding ability within reach of free-tier users and high-volume workloads at a fraction of Astra's cost per task.

item.title: New term: Grok 4.7
item.description: Grok 4.7 is xAI's September 2026 release for coding and knowledge work, held at Grok 4.6's price of $2 and $6 per million tokens with a 500K context window. It matters as a test of whether xAI can stay on the frontier: independent reading places it fifth on the Artificial Analysis index, one step behind the leaders rather than among them.

item.title: New term: Jev
item.description: Jev is TypeSafe AI's decision model, released on 15 September 2026, which takes a state and a set of options and returns a typed, calibrated choice with a confidence score in a single parallel pass instead of generating text. It matters because it is priced and built for code to call at high volume, competing on intelligence per dollar rather than on frontier capability.

item.title: New term: RLCD
item.description: RLCD, reinforcement learning for calibrated decisions, is a training method that teaches a model to answer many typed questions about a single input with calibrated probabilities in one pass, instead of generating text. It matters because it produces fast, cheap decision models whose confidence can be trusted, positioned as a replacement for preference-based training in decision work and as an alternative to using a large model as a judge.

item.title: New term: Regulatory capture
item.description: Regulatory capture, in the AI context, is the charge that safety rules proposed by leading laboratories would entrench those laboratories by raising compliance costs beyond what smaller competitors and open-model developers can bear. It matters because it is the standing objection to every pacing, licensing and coordination proposal, and it decides whether such proposals are read as public safety or as moat-building.

item.title: New term: Terminal-Bench
item.description: Terminal-Bench is a benchmark of command-line tasks that scores coding agents end to end, with version 2.1 comprising 87 tasks. It matters because agent harness research now reports cost, repeated-success and reliability figures on it rather than raw capability, making it a common yardstick for how agents are built, not only which model they run.
